ca_conspiracy_wall.blurb: Conspiracy Wall is a small wall in the Darkside sector of Fairview Mountain, near Apple Valley in the High Desert. It has seven routes split between trad and sport: four trad lines, mostly cracks, from 5.7 to 5.9, and three bolted lines running from 5.9 up to a single 5.11. The wall faces northeast, which keeps it in shade, and the ground at its base is roomy enough for a larger group. The mix suits a party where one person leads gear and another prefers clipping bolts, with most of the climbing in the 5.8 to 5.10 range.

ca_hidden_gully.blurb: Hidden Gully is a small crag on Bishop Peak, a volcanic plug above San Luis Obispo on the Central Coast. It has seven routes, and trad leads dominate: four gear lines from 5.9 to 5.11, some of which can also be top-roped. Two more routes are set up as top-ropes, one of them a beginner-level scramble and the other near 5.12, and one bolted line sits at the same hard end of the scale. The rock is dacite. It is a compact spot best suited to climbers who already lead trad at the 5.10 level.

ca_crucified_crag.blurb: Crucified Crag is one of the smaller walls in Box Canyon East, part of New Jack City in the High Desert near Barstow. All seven routes are bolted: four sit in the 5.10 range and three in the 5.11 range, so it fits climbers already comfortable on steady sport grades. The wall faces north and the volcanic rock is of good quality. Several of the lines are long and technical, with a few shorter ones mixed in.

ca_daring_boulder.blurb: Daring Boulder stands in the Central Basin of Boulder Basin on Black Mountain in the San Jacinto Mountains, at roughly 7,500 feet. It sits among the campsites and is one of the simpler boulders in the basin to locate. Seven problems cover a wide range: a couple of very easy lines at the bottom, a V3, three problems at V5, and one V10 at the top. The stone is solid and the landings are flat, though several lines climb well off the ground, so extra pads and a spotter are worth having.

ca_bovine_dome.blurb: Bovine Dome is a small formation in the Stirrup Tank West section of Pinto Basin, Joshua Tree National Park, where the road to Stirrup Tank leaves the main paved road. A short stroll from the roadside pullout reaches it. Seven climbs cover mostly low-angle terrain: six trad routes from 5.3 up to 5.10, plus a single V0 boulder problem. Most lines are at the moderate end, in the 5.3 to 5.9 range and just the one route at 5.10.

ca_crystal_corridor.blurb: Crystal Corridor is a small side canyon in the Inner Gorge of Owens River Gorge, in the Bishop area of the Eastern Sierra, at about 5,700 feet. It lies between the Dilithium Crystal formation and the main wall of the gorge. Seven short routes make up the crag: five sport and two trad, with grades running from 5.9 through the 5.10s and one 5.12. Most pitches are brief and sit in the 5.10 range. It is close to the Dilithium Crystal yet feels tucked away, with just a short scramble needed to reach the base.

ca_b_castle_rock_south_face.blurb: The South Face is the tallest and most prominent section of Castle Rock, in the San Bernardino Mountains near Big Bear Lake, at about 7,400 feet. The stone is firm and well featured. Seven routes mix four sport lines and three trad lines, with one 5.8 trad route as the easiest and most of the rest from 5.10 to 5.12. The face heats up in summer sun. A trail along the base of the rock leads to the start of the climbing.

_skipped.ca_dairy_queen_wall_upper_left_side: Its own page is only a one-line description (a ledge system above one lower-tier route); the Dairy Queen Wall parent page lists it, but there is no real standalone description to write from, and search budget ran out before other pages could be found.
